content:
Firewall Rules Logging has the following specifications:
Firewall Rules Logging can be enabled for the following:
Firewall rules in hierarchical firewall policies, regional system firewall policies,
global network firewall policies, and regional network firewall policies that are
associated with a regular VPC network.
VPC firewall rules in a regular VPC network.
Firewall rules in regional network firewall policies that are associated with an RoCE
VPC network (/firewall/docs/firewall-for-roce).
Firewall Rules Logging doesn't support the following:
VPC firewall rules in Legacy networks (/vpc/docs/legacy).
Implied deny ingress and implied allow egress rules
(/firewall/docs/firewalls#default_firewall_rules) of a regular VPC network.
Implied allow ingress and egress rules
(/firewall/docs/firewall-for-roce#implied_firewall_rules) of an RoCE VPC network.
Firewall Rules Logging only records TCP and UDP connections. Although you can create
a firewall rule that applies to other protocols (/firewall/docs/firewalls#protocols_and_ports),
you cannot log their connections. If you want to also log other protocols, consider using
Packet Mirroring (/vpc/docs/packet-mirroring).
Log entries are written from the perspective of VMs. Log entries are only created if a
firewall rule has logging enabled and if the rule applies to traffic sent to or from the VM.
Entries are created according to the connection logging limits on a best effort basis.
The number of connections that Firewall Rules Logging can log per unit of time:
Is based on machine type (/vpc/docs/quota#logging_limits) for regular VPC networks.
Depends on the monitoring or logging action of the firewall rule
(/firewall/docs/firewall-for-roce#monitoring_and_logging) for RoCE VPC networks.
Changes to firewall rules can be viewed in VPC audit logs (/vpc/docs/audit-logging).
